questions.q: Why did the admin create and switch to "Q3 Incident Routing Fix" before editing the Business Rule?
options: Editing before switching would have captured that change into whatever Update Set was previously current, usually Default
ServiceNow requires Update Sets to be created alphabetically
It has no real effect on where changes are captured
Business Rules cannot be edited until an Update Set exists
questions.explain: This is the exact ordering mistake from Lesson 30 -- changes are captured into whatever is Current at the moment they're made.

questions.q: What did the admin confirm during the review step, before marking the Update Set Complete?
options: That the Update Set contained exactly the two intended changes -- the Business Rule and the ACL -- and nothing else
That the target instance had zero users logged in
That the Business Rule had been deleted
That the Update Set had already been committed to Production
questions.explain: A clean, scoped review before Complete is what Lesson 30 recommends -- confirming no unrelated changes bled in.

questions.q: What did Preview flag on the Test instance, and why?
options: A missing dependency, because the Business Rule referenced a Script Include that didn't exist yet
A collision on the ACL, because a teammate had edited that same ACL's role requirement directly on Test
A skipped record, because the admin chose not to apply the Business Rule
Nothing -- Preview came back completely clean on both changes
questions.explain: The Business Rule was clean, but the ACL showed a real collision: two independent edits to the same configuration.

questions.q: Why did the admin merge both ACL changes instead of simply picking one version over the other?
options: ServiceNow does not allow picking only one version in any case
The two changes addressed different role requirements and weren't actually in conflict in substance, so combining both was the correct resolution
Merging is always required for every collision, regardless of content
The teammate's change had to be discarded automatically
questions.explain: Resolving a collision means reviewing both versions and deciding deliberately -- here, the right call was a merge, not an automatic pick.

questions.q: What did the admin do only after the Business Rule was confirmed clean and the ACL collision was deliberately resolved?
options: Delete the Update Set from Dev
Commit the Update Set on Test and retest with realistic data before moving toward Production
Skip Test entirely and commit directly to Production
Revert the Business Rule back to its original version
questions.explain: Committing only happens after Preview issues are resolved, and Production is never reached by skipping Test's validation.
